payload.report: The patient’s progressive exertional dyspnea, pedal edema, tachycardia, and JVD initially pointed to heart failure/volume overload. Echocardiography showing EF 15-20% with grade 2 diastolic dysfunction plus markedly elevated BNP at 1700 pg/mL definitively support HFrEF (node-9), which in turn supports volume overload (node-4). The same objective findings refute primary pulmonary hypertension and primary renal disease; any pulmonary hypertension is secondary to left heart failure (node-10). Thus the most probable diagnosis is HFrEF causing volume overload and secondary pulmonary hypertension.
